To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the insight obtained by studying the electrochemically promoted catalytic reduction of nitrogen oxides by hydrocarbons over Pt-film catalysts has been used to design conventional-type catalyst formulations for the same reactions that exhibit similar performance and behaviour.

the electrochemical promotion (EP) effect, also known as non-Faradaic electrochemical modification of catalytic activity (NEMCA), can be used to enhance the catalytic performance of a variety of catalytic reactions, and that this enhancement can be used to guide the development of conventional catalysts.

electrochemical promotion of Pt-film and Pt dispersed catalysts is very similar and that the insight obtained by EP can be used to develop effective Pt catalyst formulations for the reduction of NO by hydrocarbons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of electrochemistry and electrochemical techniques to the design of novel catalysts, the understanding of the mechanism of catalysis, and the development of novel catalytic processes.
the design of effective catalysts and catalyst formulations by the use of the electrochemical promotion (EP) phenomenon, discovered and developed by our group.
the development and application of electrochemical techniques in the field of heterogeneous catalysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EP, or NEMCA, is a new and highly controllable method for catalyst promotion, with the potential for application in many catalytic systems.
EP is a very useful tool for catalyst design.
the EP (NEMCA) phenomenon is a novel, in situ, reversible, highly controllable, and very efficient means of catalyst promotion that can be used for the design of effective catalyst formulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EP effect has provided us with the ability to study the promotion mechanism of a catalyst in an in-situ manner and to understand the effect of the promoter on the catalyst.

we have demonstrated that the electrochemical promotion of catalysis (EPOC) is not a phenomenon that occurs only in electrochemical cells, but is a real phenomenon that also occurs in the real world of catalysis, where it can be used to improve catalytic performance.
the electrochemical promotion (NEMCA) phenomenon is a powerful new method for the design of effective catalysts, and that it provides a new tool for the study of catalytic reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can design effective catalysts by applying our understanding of the electrochemical promotion effect.
we can use electrochemical promotion to design conventional catalysts that are more active and selective than the conventional ones.
we have demonstrated that the insight obtained by electrochemical promotion studies can be used as a guide to design effective catalyst formulations that are otherwise difficult to conceive.
